title: Rachel and Leah (Genesis 29:1–30)
hookLine: seven years feel like a few days for love, then the deceiver is deceived
last: GOD WAS HERE AND I DIDN'T KNOW.

cards: Jacob reaches a well in the east. Shepherds stand around it, waiting, because the stone over its mouth is too heavy to move until all the flocks gather. Then a young woman walks up with her father's sheep.
Her name is Rachel, and she is his cousin. Jacob, who has walked for days, rolls the stone off by himself, waters her flock, kisses her, and bursts into tears. Her father Laban takes him in.
After a month, Laban asks what wages he wants. Jacob already knows. Not money.

teach.h: SEVEN YEARS, LIKE A FEW DAYS.
teach.b: Jacob offers seven years of work for her. In the King James Bible: "Jacob served seven years for Rachel; and they seemed unto him but a few days, for the love he had to her." Love does strange things to a clock.
In the dark, the bride is not Rachel. Laban has sent in her older sister, Leah. In the morning, the man who wore goat skins to fool his blind father finds out what it is to be fooled.
"What is this thou hast done unto me?"
Laban's answer is cool: in our country we don't give the younger before the firstborn. That's exactly what Jacob did to Esau. Genesis never says the word payback.
It lets you hear it. Jacob marries Rachel a week later, and works seven more years.
But don't skip Leah. The text says Jacob loved Rachel more, and that God saw Leah was unloved.

teach.h: FOR THE LOVE HE HAD TO HER.
teach.b: Her sons get names full of her hope that her husband will finally love her. One of them is Judah. From Judah's line come King David and, in Matthew's family tree, Jesus.

The woman Jacob didn't choose is not forgotten by the story. Read honestly, this is a hurting family, not a model marriage: two sisters, one husband, a father who uses them both. The love is real, and so is the pain.

how: Genesis 29:20 is sometimes read at weddings and anniversaries, and Rachel and Leah are remembered in Christian and Jewish tradition as mothers of Israel; Ruth 4:11 names them together in a blessing.

games.q: you're Jacob. you wake after the wedding and find Leah beside you, not Rachel. Laban says the older sister goes first. what do you do?

games.why: he agrees, marries Rachel a week later, and works seven more years. the man who tricked his father has been tricked, and he stays.

practice: Remember a stretch of life that should have felt long: caring for a parent, a long-distance year, a hard job taken for someone else's sake, a baby who wouldn't sleep.
Recall how the time actually felt, and who you were doing it for, the long and the light of it together. If you pray, you can give thanks for the person who made it feel short.

wordCard.voice: Rachel. Hebrew for a ewe, fitting for a shepherdess: the sister Jacob loved at first sight, after serving seven years that felt like a few days.

orig.note: Hebrew: Rachel. the same Hebrew word means a ewe, a fitting name for a shepherdess.
